label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
Hi Mikaela, yep we started on 21 September, after mating had started. Happy to give you the warts and all, especially after how much you helped us when Dave did his shoulder.

We’re milking 290, mostly three-way crossbreds. We’ve dropped Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday arvo milkings, so four once-a-days a week. Still 5.15 every morning, so don’t go thinking we’re having sleep-ins 😂 Cows took it better than I expected. About four days of bellowing at the gate and then they settled down.

Production-wise, going off the Fonterra app we’re about 6% down on milksolids against the same weeks last year. Our rep had said to expect 8–10%, so it’s been less of a hit than we’d braced for. That’s only a comparison with last year though, not proof the milking change accounts for all of it. And we haven’t done a full season yet, so I can’t tell you what it’ll look like by March.

Cells did jump. We were about 110,000 and went up to around 180,000 in the first three weeks. Back around 135,000 now. So they didn’t go completely mental, but I wouldn’t say there was nothing to worry about either.

The worst bit was a heifer with mastitis that went bad on a skipped arvo. We didn’t pick it up till the next morning and she lost a quarter. I don’t want to gloss over that. You’ve really got to be on your game with teat spraying and checking cows on the days you skip. An arvo out of the shed can’t mean nobody looks at the cows. It will bite you.

On the good side, lame cows are way down. Four on the list now compared with eleven this time last year. Our back paddocks are a 1.8km walk, so less walking is no small thing here.

And the difference for us has been huge. First Sunday arvo we skipped, Dave and I went to Hamilton to see the grandkids. First Sunday arvo off in spring in twenty-odd years. Kieran, our 2IC, said it’s the first spring he hasn’t wanted to quit by October. That probably tells you more about the hours than I can.

Honestly, I wouldn’t go back. For us the time is worth the 6%. With Tom’s knees as bad as they are, I reckon those arvos off could make a real difference, and possibly for your young fella too. But I wouldn’t promise you our numbers, or tell you it’s all upside. There’s less milking, but you still need to keep a close eye on things.

Come and grab me at the Kerrisons’ field day on the 19th. I’ll bring our shed rosters and numbers so you can have a proper look rather than just taking my word for it. Or ring me anytime if you want to talk it through. Much easier than texting with these useless thumbs!
